name: Rinchenpong village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,200 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Family homestays spread along the ridge between Rinchenpong bazaar, the old monastery and Kaluk. Simple rooms, home cooking and Kangchenjunga outside the window on a clear morning, at a price that leaves room in a budget trip for a car day to Barsey or Pelling.
body: Rinchenpong has no big hotels, and that is the point. A few dozen households along the road above the bazaar and on the paths towards the monastery rent out two to five rooms each, usually with attached bathrooms and hot water from a geyser or a bucket. Dinner is what the family eats: rice, dal, a seasonal vegetable such as squash or mustard greens, pickles, and chicken if you ask in advance. The district administration lists several of these homestays on soreng.nic.in, which is a useful starting point.

We match guests to a house by what they need: ground-floor rooms for older travellers, a view room for photographers, a quiet lane for couples. Standards vary from house to house, so we visit and recheck the ones we use each season rather than naming one family here. Expect power cuts in the monsoon, thin mobile data on some networks and very early mornings, because the mountain is clearest between 5:30 and 8:00 am from October to April.
why: The cheapest way to wake up facing Kangchenjunga in this part of Sikkim
Walking distance to Rinchenpong Monastery and the Rabindra Smriti Van park
Home-cooked Nepali meals made with produce from the family's own terraces

faqs.q: How much does a homestay in Rinchenpong cost?
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹1,200–2,200 per person a night with breakfast and dinner, twin sharing, in 2026. Lunch is usually extra at ₹150–250. Rates go up in October–November and around Christmas and New Year, and drop in the July–August monsoon. These are indicative figures, so check the current rate when you book or ask us to hold a room for you.

faqs.q: Do Rinchenpong homestays have attached bathrooms and hot water?
faqs.a: Most rooms we use have an attached bathroom with a western toilet and hot water from a geyser, though a few older houses still bring hot water in a bucket. Ask before you book if this matters. Heating is rare; you get thick quilts instead, which are enough from October to March when nights fall to about 3–8 °C.

faqs.q: Can we see Kangchenjunga from the homestays?
faqs.a: From many houses on the upper road, yes, on clear mornings. The best chances are October to early December and February to April, between sunrise and about 8 am. From June to September clouds usually hide the range for days at a time. If the view matters most, ask us for a house facing north-west towards the range.

name: Yangsum Heritage Farm
price_band: ≈ ₹6,000–9,500 a room a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A family farmhouse built in 1833 and remodelled in 1966, on a 44-acre organic farm about 2 km from Rinchenpong bazaar. Wood-panelled rooms, meals from the farm and guided walks make it the most characterful stay in Soreng district.
body: Yangsum is a working farm first. The family grows maize, paddy, millet, potatoes, garlic, turmeric and sweet potato, and the kitchen cooks with what comes in from the fields that week. The main house, built in 1833 and remodelled in 1966 according to the hosts and several travel features, keeps its old wooden panelling, and the guest rooms have private bathrooms. The farm sits at roughly 1,500 m, below Rinchenpong, with the Kangchenjunga range to the north-west.

It suits travellers who want to slow down for two or three nights: walk the farm paths, eat long meals, and take a locally guided day hike towards the monastery or the villages below. It is not a resort, so do not expect a spa, a bar or room service. Rooms are few and book out early for October–November and spring, so plan two to three months ahead for those weeks.
why: A real 19th-century Sikkimese farmhouse rather than a new concrete block
Food grown on the farm, cooked the way the family eats it
Guided walks that connect the farm to Rinchenpong's monasteries and villages

faqs.q: How far is Yangsum Heritage Farm from Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: About 2 km from Rinchenpong bazaar, a few minutes by car or a 30–40 minute walk on village paths. Rinchenpong Monastery is a short drive or a steady uphill walk away. Your car can reach the farm, but if you arrive by shared jeep, call ahead so the hosts can tell you where to get off.

faqs.q: Is Yangsum Heritage Farm worth the higher price?
faqs.a: If you value history, home-grown food and quiet, yes. You pay for a family farmhouse from 1833, guided walks and meals from the fields rather than for luxury fittings. Travellers who want a television, a bar or a lift will be happier at a resort in Kaluk. We suggest two nights so you can join a farm walk without rushing.

faqs.q: Is Yangsum suitable for children and older travellers?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The farm has open space, animals and easy paths, which children enjoy. Older travellers should ask for a room with the fewest steps, since the house and farm are on a slope. There is no medical facility on site; the nearest clinics are in Rinchenpong and Soreng, and the district hospital is in Soreng.

name: Ghonday Village Resort
summary: A long-running village resort on the road below Rinchenpong in Kaluk, listed by the Soreng district administration. Cottage-style rooms, a restaurant and garden terraces facing the Kangchenjunga range make it a reliable middle-budget base for Kaluk and Rinchenpong.
body: Ghonday sits on the slope between Kaluk and Rinchenpong, and is one of the stays the Soreng district website lists for visitors. Rooms are spread across the hillside in low buildings rather than one block, with a dining room serving Indian, Nepali and simple continental food. On clear mornings the range from Kabru to Pandim lines up across the valley, and the garden is the place to watch it.

We use it for families and couples who want private bathrooms, a restaurant on site and a car park at the door, without paying hill-station hotel prices. It is a short drive to Rinchenpong Monastery, the Rabindra Smriti Van park and Kaluk bazaar, and about 1.5 hours to Barsey's trailhead at Hilley if you go via Soreng. Rates move with the season; spring and autumn weekends fill first.
why: Private rooms, a restaurant and parking without hill-station prices
Garden terraces facing the Kangchenjunga range
Central for Kaluk, Rinchenpong and day trips towards Soreng

faqs.q: Where exactly is Ghonday Village Resort?
faqs.a: It is on the Kaluk side of the road below Rinchenpong, in Soreng district, about 32 km from Jorethang and roughly 31 km from Pelling via Gyalshing and Legship. Kaluk bazaar and Rinchenpong are each a few minutes' drive away. Drivers from Jorethang and Pelling know it by name, so you will not need directions.

faqs.q: What does a room at Ghonday Village Resort cost?
faqs.a: As an indicative 2026 band, expect about ₹3,000–5,500 a room a night for two, depending on room type and season, with breakfast sometimes included. October–November, Christmas–New Year and April are the dearest weeks. Check the current rate directly or ask us, since resorts here change prices each season.

faqs.q: Is Ghonday good for a family with grandparents?
faqs.a: Yes, with one caution: the property is on a slope, so some rooms need a short climb. Ask for a room near the dining area and the car park. There is space to sit outdoors, food is served on site, and the drive from Jorethang is about 1.5 hours, which is gentler than the longer roads to Pelling or North Sikkim.

name: Mandarin Village Resort
summary: A hillside resort on the Kaluk–Rinchenpong road near Kaluk bazaar, spread over terraced grounds with mountain views. It suits families and couples who want a restaurant, parking and walking space, five minutes from the bazaar and a short drive from Rinchenpong Monastery.
body: Mandarin Village Resort is on the Kaluk–Rinchenpong road near Kaluk bazaar, with rooms set across terraced grounds and a restaurant that serves Indian and local dishes. The name fits the district, which is known for its oranges, ginger and large cardamom. Booking sites list it from roughly ₹2,500–3,000 a room in the low season.

It is a practical value choice: the car can drop you at the door, the bazaar is close for snacks and medicines, and evenings are quiet. In clear weather the Kangchenjunga range shows up across the valley from the grounds. Kaluk is known as one of the windier spots in Sikkim, so pack a windproof layer for evenings from November to February. Expect rate changes by season and confirm what meals are included before you pay.
why: Close to Kaluk bazaar yet quiet after dark
Terraced grounds with space for children to walk around
Easy drive to Rinchenpong Monastery and the Rabindra Smriti Van park

faqs.q: How far is Mandarin Village Resort from Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: About 3 km by road, roughly ten minutes by car. It lies on the Kaluk–Rinchenpong road near Kaluk bazaar. Rinchenpong Monastery is a little further uphill, about 15–20 minutes by car. Most guests use it as a base and visit Rinchenpong, the Rabindra Smriti Van park and Sribadam on short drives.

faqs.q: Can we see Kangchenjunga from Mandarin Village Resort?
faqs.a: On clear days, yes, across the valley to the north-west. The best months are October to December and February to April, early in the morning. From June to September cloud usually covers the range. If the view is important, ask for an upper-terrace room when you book, and check current room availability before you travel.

faqs.q: Is food available at Mandarin Village Resort?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a restaurant on site serving Indian dishes and local food such as momos, thukpa and rice-dal meals. Vegetarian and Jain requests are usually possible with notice. Confirm whether your rate includes breakfast only or breakfast and dinner, since packages differ. Kaluk bazaar nearby has a few simple eateries and shops too.

name: Okhrey Sherpa village homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Homestays run by Sherpa families in Okhrey, a village of about 2,300 m below Hilley, the road gateway to Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary. Wood-lined rooms, Sherpa and Nepali home food and a Nyingma monastery up the hill make it the best budget base for Barsey.
body: Okhrey is a mainly Sherpa village, and over the last two decades many families have opened rooms to travellers heading for the Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary. Houses are typically two or three storeys, with wood-panelled rooms that stay warm, attached bathrooms in most newer rooms and meals in the family kitchen: rice, dal, vegetables from the garden, eggs and, on request, Sherpa dishes such as thenthuk or potato-based meals. Ugen Thondroling Monastery, built in 1950 and following the Nyingma school, sits above the village.

Hilley, where the 4–4.5 km trail to Barsey begins, is about 8 km up the road, so most guests take a car at dawn, walk to the ridge and come back for a late lunch. Rooms fill in late March to May when the rhododendrons bloom, so book early for those weeks. October to December brings clearer views of the range and fewer people.
why: The closest village base to the Hilley–Barsey trail
Sherpa family homes with a 1950 Nyingma monastery up the hill
Budget prices that include dinner and breakfast

faqs.q: Why stay in Okhrey instead of Hilley?
faqs.a: Okhrey has many more homestays, more food choice, a village to walk around and a monastery, while Hilley is little more than a checkpost and a few houses. Okhrey is also lower, at about 2,300 m against 2,750 m at Hilley, so nights are a little milder. The drive up to the Hilley trailhead is only about 8 km, 30–40 minutes.

faqs.q: When are Okhrey homestays fully booked?
faqs.a: Late March to early May, when rhododendrons bloom in the Barsey sanctuary, is the busiest period, and spring weekends sell out first. Book four to eight weeks ahead for that season. October to December is quieter and better for mountain views. From June to September most travellers stay away because of rain and leeches on the trail.

faqs.q: How cold is Okhrey in winter?
faqs.a: From December to February, night temperatures can fall to around 0–4 °C and frost is common; snow falls on the higher Barsey ridge in some winters. Homestays give thick quilts but rarely have heaters, so bring thermals, a warm hat and socks. Days are usually clear and sunny, which makes winter good for views if you dress for it.

name: Sherpa Lodge
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–1,800 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A family-run Sherpa homestay in Okhrey, about 30 minutes by car from the Hilley checkpost. Seven wood-panelled rooms with attached bathrooms, all meals included and an upstairs patio facing the hills make it a dependable budget base for the Barsey walk.
body: Sherpa Lodge is one of the better-known homestays in Okhrey, run by a local Sherpa family. Travel writers who stayed there describe a two-storey building with seven bedrooms, wood panelling for warmth and attached bathrooms, with an upstairs patio that looks over the hills. Rates have usually included breakfast, lunch, evening tea and dinner, with vegetables from the family's own garden.

It is about 10 km from Sombaria and around 30 minutes by road from the Hilley checkpost, which makes a dawn start for Barsey easy to arrange. The family can help book a car to Hilley. Rooms go quickly in April and May, the rhododendron season, so reserve well ahead. As with every homestay, standards and prices change; check current status before you travel or ask us to confirm.
why: All meals included at a budget price
Warm wood-lined rooms with attached bathrooms
Thirty minutes from the Barsey trailhead at Hilley

faqs.q: What is included in the Sherpa Lodge rate?
faqs.a: The usual rate has been around ₹1,200 per person a night including breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner, with lower prices off-season. For 2026 we budget ₹1,200–1,800 per person. Confirm what is included when you book, since rates can change with demand, especially in April and May.

faqs.q: How do we get from Sherpa Lodge to Barsey?
faqs.a: Take a car up to the Hilley checkpost, about 30 minutes, pay the sanctuary entry fee there and walk 4–4.5 km to the Barsey ridge, usually 1.5–2 hours up. The family can arrange the car, which typically costs ₹600–800 one way. Many guests walk back down and are collected at Hilley around midday.

faqs.q: Is Sherpa Lodge suitable for vegetarians?
faqs.a: Yes. Home meals here are mostly rice, dal and vegetables grown in the garden, so vegetarian food is the default and eggs or chicken are extras. Tell the family in advance if you need no onion or garlic, or have other dietary rules. Bring snacks for the trail, since there is little to buy above Hilley.

name: Hilley and Barsey trailhead homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,000–1,800 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A handful of small family homestays at Hilley, around 2,750 m at the road-end entrance to Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary. Basic rooms and hot meals, with the forest trail starting outside, for walkers who want to be on the ridge at sunrise.
body: Hilley is a checkpost, a few houses and the start of the trail into Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary. The Soreng district website lists several homestays at the sanctuary entrance, among them Barsey Residency Homestay, Lali Gurash Homestay and Royal Barsey Homestay, and a few more families take guests in season. Rooms are simple, bathrooms may be shared in some houses and meals are rice, dal, vegetables and eggs, served hot.

The reason to sleep here rather than in Okhrey is the early start: you can be on the trail at first light and on the Barsey ridge for the morning view of Kangchenjunga before cloud builds up. At about 2,750 m, Hilley is cold year-round at night, with frost from November to February. Electricity and mobile signal can be unreliable, so charge devices when you can and carry a torch.
why: Sleep at the trailhead and walk into Barsey at first light
Hot home meals at the edge of the forest
The cheapest beds on the Barsey route

faqs.q: Are there homestays at Hilley?
faqs.a: Yes, a few small family homestays sit near the Hilley checkpost and the sanctuary entrance; the Soreng district website lists Barsey Residency, Lali Gurash and Royal Barsey homestays among them. They are basic, with limited rooms, so book ahead for March to May. Okhrey, 8 km below, has far more choice if Hilley is full.

faqs.q: How cold does it get at Hilley at night?
faqs.a: Hilley is about 2,750 m, so expect night temperatures near 0–5 °C from November to March and around 8–12 °C even in April and May. Frost is common in winter. Bring a fleece, a down or padded jacket, a warm hat and thermals. Homestays give heavy quilts but usually no room heating.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay at Hilley or walk up from Okhrey?
faqs.a: Stay at Hilley if a sunrise view from the Barsey ridge is your priority, since you start walking at dawn. Choose Okhrey for more comfort, more food choice and a village to explore, then drive 8 km up to Hilley early in the morning. Either way, the walk from Hilley to the ridge is 4–4.5 km.

name: The Orchid Hotel
summary: A plain town hotel at Pragati Chowk in Soreng, the district headquarters, listed by the Soreng district administration. Practical private rooms for a night in town before Chuli Dara at sunrise, Tharpu's Mangardzong or the road west to Okhrey and Hilley.
body: Soreng is a working district town rather than a resort, and The Orchid Hotel is one of the commercial hotels the district website lists, at Pragati Chowk near the bazaar. Expect simple private rooms and basic service rather than views or extras. We use it when a journey needs a night in Soreng: for an early walk up Chuli Dara, a morning at Tharpu and Mangardzong, or as a halfway stop between Rinchenpong and Okhrey.

The advantage is location. Shared jeeps leave from the bazaar for Jorethang and Siliguri, there are pharmacies, ATMs and small eateries a short walk away, and the district hospital is in town. Book a room on the quieter side if you can, since the bazaar wakes early. As with all town hotels, check current rates and what is included before you travel.
why: In Soreng bazaar, close to shared jeeps, ATMs and pharmacies
A practical overnight for Chuli Dara, Tharpu and Mangardzong
Private rooms at a budget price

faqs.q: Is it worth staying a night in Soreng town?
faqs.a: If you want to walk up Chuli Dara for sunrise, visit Tharpu and the Mangardzong site, or break the long road between Rinchenpong and Okhrey, yes. Soreng has banks, pharmacies and shared jeeps, which Rinchenpong and Okhrey lack. For views and quiet, most travellers prefer to sleep in Rinchenpong, Kaluk or Okhrey.

faqs.q: How far is Soreng from Jorethang and Siliguri?
faqs.a: Soreng is about 28 km from Jorethang, roughly an hour by road, and about 100 km from Siliguri, around 4 hours via Melli and Jorethang. The Siliguri–Melli stretch follows NH10 along the Teesta, which closes after landslides in the monsoon; the alternative is via Kalimpong. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does The Orchid Hotel serve food?
faqs.a: Check when you book, since services at small town hotels change. Either way, Soreng bazaar has several simple eateries serving momos, thukpa, chowmein and rice-dal thalis for about ₹120–250. Breakfast places open early because shared jeeps leave for Jorethang and Siliguri from around 6–7 am.
